chunks: From him, from Ibn Asbat, from Al-Hasan ibn Jaham who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a matter of relief (Faraj). He replied: Do you not know that waiting for the relief is from the relief? I said: I do not know, except what you teach me. He said: Yes, waiting for the relief is from the relief.

key_terms.أَبِي اَلْحَسَنُ: Abu Al-Hasan (Imam Al-Hadi, peace be upon him)
key_terms.اَلْفَرَج: Relief, deliverance, or opening (of a difficult situation)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of waiting (Intizar) for the relief of the Imam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Al-Hadi (a.s.) elucidates the profound spiritual status of *Intizar al-Faraj* (waiting for relief), teaching that the active, expectant state of the faithful is not merely passive waiting but is itself counted as a divine favor or 'relief.' This concept underscores the Shia theological principle that the psychological and spiritual preparation for the Imam's return constitutes a tangible part of the deliverance process, reinforcing the merit of steadfastness during the period of occultation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 471 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Ibn Asbat from Hasan bin Jaham that he said:

“I asked His Eminence, Abul Hasan Musa bin Ja’far (a.s) regarding relief (Faraj). He replied: Don’t you know that waiting for the Faraj is Faraj? I asked: I don’t know anything, except what you have taught. He replied: Yes, waiting for the Faraj is (also) a kind of Faraj.”
